_about: Gerber Bear benchmark. Each case is a request written the way a user would type it, the facts the simulated user knows (used only to answer the assistant's questions), and what a correct outcome is. expect: build = a proposal must be reached and match the checks; refuse = no proposal, the request must be declined with an explanation; build_or_explain = a matching proposal, or no proposal with the limit explained. never_invent lists spec fields the first message does not state: the assistant must ask, not fill them in.

cases.prompt: I need a Wi-Fi controller for four 12V PC fans, each up to 0.3A, with a temperature probe.
cases.facts: Supply is a 12 V adapter. No size limit. Any number of layers is fine.

cases.prompt: Board to drive 8 LED strips at 24V, 0.8A each, controlled from my Raspberry Pi over I2C.
cases.facts: The Pi provides the I2C bus. Power is a 24 V supply.

cases.prompt: ESP32 greenhouse board: a humidity sensor, two 12V solenoid valves at 0.4A, and 4 analog inputs for soil moisture probes.
cases.facts: 12 V supply. The moisture probes output 0 to 3 V.

cases.prompt: Make me a board to control some lights.
cases.facts: Six 12 V LED strips, 0.5 A each, controlled over Wi-Fi from my phone. 12 V power supply.

cases.prompt: 16 channel 12V relay coil driver, 80mA per coil, ESP32 controlled. 4 layers is fine.
cases.facts: 12 V supply.

cases.prompt: Small board, exactly 100 x 70 mm: ESP32, two 12V heaters at 0.9A each and a DS18B20.
cases.facts: 12 V supply, 2 layers preferred.

cases.prompt: ESP32 board that switches three 12V solenoids.
cases.facts: Each solenoid draws 0.6 A. 12 V supply.

cases.prompt: 24V input, ESP32, two DC fans at 1.5A each.
cases.facts: The fans really need 1.5 A each at start-up.

cases.prompt: I want 40 MOSFET outputs for 12V LEDs, 0.2A each, from an ESP32.
cases.facts: 12 V supply. Exactly 40 outputs.

cases.prompt: USB-C powered ESP32 board I can program over the same USB cable, with two 5V LED outputs at 0.5A.
cases.facts: Power comes only from USB-C, 5 V.

cases.prompt: Battery powered sensor node: one Li-ion cell charged from USB-C, ESP32, humidity and temperature sensor.
cases.facts: Single 18650 or pouch cell, 3.7 V nominal. No switched outputs.

cases.prompt: Drive two brushed DC motors forward and reverse, 12V up to 1A each, from an ESP32.
cases.facts: 12 V supply. Speed control by PWM.

cases.prompt: ESP32 board with 4 relays to switch 24V DC valves, 2A per valve, 12V supply for the board.
cases.facts: The valves have their own 24 V supply wired through the relay contacts.

cases.prompt: RS-485 Modbus node: ESP32, 24V supply, 4 MOSFET outputs for 24V lamps at 0.3A.
cases.facts: Half-duplex RS-485 with a screw terminal and a termination resistor jumper.

cases.prompt: CAN bus sensor node with an ESP32, 12V supply, BME280 environment sensor.
cases.facts: CAN at 500 kbit/s, screw terminal for CANH/CANL.

cases.prompt: 12V ESP32 board with a connector for a small I2C OLED display and a BME280 sensor.
cases.facts: A standard 4-pin 0.96 inch SSD1306 OLED module.

cases.prompt: 24V supply but the 6 LED strips run at 12V, 0.5A each, ESP32 controlled.
cases.facts: There is a separate 12 V supply for the strips.

cases.prompt: 12V barrel jack powered ESP32 board with 2 fan outputs, 0.25A each.
cases.facts: Standard 5.5 x 2.1 mm barrel jack.

cases.prompt: Design a mains-powered 230V AC to 5V 2A power supply board.
cases.facts: It plugs straight into the wall.

cases.prompt: I need an FPGA board with DDR4 memory and PCIe.
cases.facts: Xilinx Artix-7, 1 GB DDR4.

cases.prompt: Make a 2.4 GHz RF power amplifier with a custom PCB antenna.
cases.facts: 20 dBm output.
